- When sentiment is positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion or downward momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral, model often underestimates; increase forecast to reflect potential rebound or bullish reversal.
- Model frequently overshoots after recent price spikes (especially in 30d horizon), suggesting overreaction; apply dampening factor or lag correction for spikes.
- In 30d forecasts, model shows persistent bias toward lower prices when sentiment is weak; adjust upward if sentiment turns positive within 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows multiple 1.00 entries (strong bullish sentiment), model often fails to capture sustained rally; increase forecast by 2–5% for 10–15 day horizons.
- Model underreacts to sentiment shifts in early days of a new trend; delay forecast adjustment until sentiment stabilizes or moves >0.33 in 3 consecutive days.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome shows sharp decline after a spike, model often fails to anticipate; add lagged correction: subtract 10–15% of previous 7d average if sentiment drops sharply.
